You’re set up to proceed; the handoff indicates there’s a current champion (`baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`), no PASS candidates, and nothing currently INCONCLUSIVE. The next actionable step is simply to run the three commands in order to (1) search/select best module-level candidates, (2) run system-level candidates, and (3) generate a “next fix” report.

## What to do next (run in order)

```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```

## What to look for after each step

1) **`aub_autopilot.py ... --select-best`**
- Expected outcome: it should evaluate module candidates and either:
  - promote a new best candidate (creating/marking a PASS), or
  - keep the champion if nothing beats it / meets gates.
- If it still yields “no PASS candidates,” note which modules are repeatedly failing and whether failures are due to mean vs min thresholds (your current min for tuning is quite low: `0.431`).

2) **`system_autopilot.py ...`**
- Expected outcome: end-to-end/system candidates get evaluated.
- Check whether any candidate improves both **mean and min** (or whatever gating criteria your system uses) relative to the current champion.

3) **`aub_next_fix.py ... --output ...`**
- Expected outcome: it writes `baseline/reports/next_fix.md`.
- This should summarize the most likely fixes to pursue next (e.g., flaky tests, regressions concentrated in particular tasks, modules with highest ROI).

## Quick sanity checks (before/after running)
- Ensure you’re on the intended commit/branch and have a clean working tree:
  - `git status`
- Confirm results are being written where you expect (some setups default to a run directory).
- If runs are stochastic, verify seeds/repeats match your usual gating policy.

If you paste the stdout/stderr (or just the “best candidate / failures summary” sections) from the first command, I can help interpret why there are no PASS candidates yet and what the next fix report is likely to recommend.
